## 3: 
```{python}
from sys import exit 

def get_mealplan_data(x): 
    if x<=100 or x>=210:
        exit("enter a valid number")
    x=str(x)
    URL2 = "https://tastesbetterfromscratch.com/meal-plan-" + x + "/"
    HEADERS2 = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)"}

    response2 = requests.get(URL2, headers=HEADERS2)
    soup2 = BeautifulSoup(response2.content, "html.parser")


    rows2 = []

    for week in soup2.find_all("p", {"class": "has-text-align-left"}):
        # Find the course name tag
        day_name = week.find("strong")
        day = day_name.get_text(strip = True)

        recipe_name = week.find("a")
        recipe = recipe_name.get_text(strip = True)

        recipe_link = recipe_name.get("href")

        recipe_price=re.findall(r"\$.{2,5}(?=</p>)",str(week))
        price=recipe_price[0]

        rows2.append({
            "day": day,
            "recipe": recipe,
            "recipe_link": recipe_link,
            "price": price
        })

    df2=pd.DataFrame(rows2)
    df2["day"] = df2["day"].apply(lambda x: x.replace(":", ""))
    
    def tasty_recipe(y):
        url = "https://tasty.p.rapidapi.com/recipes/list" #this is the endpoint that you are getting info from 

        querystring = {"from":"0","size":"20","q":y}

        headers = {
            "X-RapidAPI-Key": "9d224792admshacbb1b5b61365fbp161a09jsn8429ec576154",
            "X-RapidAPI-Host": "tasty.p.rapidapi.com"
        }

        response3 = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=querystring) #this wont look pretty

        y_recipes = pd.json_normalize(response3.json(), "results")
        #print(y_recipes)
        #y_recipes=y_recipes[["canonical_id", "name", "num_servings", "nutrition.calories", "nutrition.carbohydrates", "nutrition.fat", "nutrition.fiber", "nutrition.protein", "nutrition.sugar", "price.portion", "price.total"]]
        
        if y_recipes.empty:
            return y_recipes
        else: 
            y_recipes=y_recipes[["canonical_id", "name", "num_servings", "nutrition.calories", "nutrition.carbohydrates", "nutrition.fat", "nutrition.fiber", "nutrition.protein", "nutrition.sugar", "price.portion", "price.total"]]
            y_recipes.loc[:, "recipe"] = y
            return y_recipes
    
    tasty_rec_total = pd.DataFrame()

    for i in ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday"]:
        y = df2.loc[df2["day"] == i, "recipe"].iloc[0]
        tasty_rec_total=pd.concat([tasty_rec_total,tasty_recipe(y)])          

# single left merge back onto your meal plan
    total_df = df2.merge(tasty_rec_total, on="recipe", how="left")

    return total_df
```

```{python}
week202=get_mealplan_data(202)
week202.head()
```

## 4: 
```{python}
import numpy as np 

#this is my list of "common" meats to check in each recipe title 
meats=np.array(["chicken", "beef", "steak", "turkey", "salmon", "pork", "meat", "lamb", "fish", "shrimp", "seafood", "salmon"])
```

```{python}
import re
from numpy import isin 

def is_veg(x): 
    x=x.lower()
    recipe_list=np.array(x.split(" "))
    is_vegetarian=isin(recipe_list, meats)
    if is_vegetarian.sum()==0:
        return "Vegetarian"
    else: 
        return "Contains meat"
```

```{python}
is_veg("sadie chicken salad")
```

```{python}
week202['name'] = week202['name'].fillna('No recipe found')
week202['vegetarian']=week202["name"].apply(is_veg)
week202.head()
week202[["name", "vegetarian"]].head()
```


## 5: 
```{python}
week202_cleaned=week202.dropna()
week202_cleaned.head()
```

```{python}
import plotnine as p9

(p9.ggplot(week202_cleaned, p9.aes(x = "vegetarian", y = "nutrition.protein", fill = "vegetarian"))
+ p9.geom_boxplot()
)
```

This visualization shows that for recipes on Tasty's website, there are a large range of vegetarian options for almost every day of the week except for Friday's meal. Additionally, Tuesday's vegetarian options have a protein content comperable to the meat version. 

```{python}
import plotnine as p9

(p9.ggplot(week202_cleaned, p9.aes(x = "nutrition.protein", y = "nutrition.fat", color = "vegetarian"))
+ p9.geom_point()
)
```

In this visualization we can see that there are more vegetarian meal options than meals that contain meat in this week's mealplan. Additionally, for recipes with the same protein content, recipes containing meat tend to have a lower fat content than vegetarian recipes.
